title: Operationalize + test living-person takedown path end-to-end
context: The living-person takedown workflow was documented in privacy-001 and the explorer is now live. The workflow must be operationalized — a real report mechanism exists and is linked from the explorer — and tested end-to-end using a synthetic living-person inclusion to verify the <=72h SLA can be met. Any confirmed living-person publication is a P0 incident requiring immediate export pull, so the path must be fast, reliable, and logged without re-publishing PII.
objective: Operationalize the living-person takedown path by adding a report mechanism to the explorer, testing the full report-to-removal flow end-to-end with a synthetic living-person inclusion, confirming the <=72h SLA is achievable, and committing a post-exercise report documenting any gaps found and remediated.
acceptanceCriteria: A low-friction report mechanism is available on the explorer (e.g., a clearly labelled link or form) and documented in the project README.
A synthetic living-person record is injected into a test environment and a takedown report filed through the live report mechanism.
The report-to-removal flow is exercised end-to-end: report received, verified, record removed from corpus and exports, removal logged without re-publishing PII.
End-to-end elapsed time measured and confirmed achievable within <=72h SLA under realistic conditions.
Source batch re-audited after synthetic removal to confirm no other synthetic or real living-person records remain.
Post-exercise report documents: time at each step, any friction points found, and any remediation actions taken.
Post-exercise report committed as docs/takedown-test-report.md via PR; report mechanism linked from explorer.
output: docs/takedown-test-report.md — end-to-end takedown test report with timeline, gaps found, and remediation actions, committed via PR; takedown report mechanism live on the explorer.
